**Week of Oct 19** · Paired lecture: *Insect-scale flapping* · No module Oct 12
:::

## What you do today

Choose your wing and tail geometry. You simulate candidate geometries in Ptera
and pick the one that gives the best thrust profile when compounded with the
provided motor power curve. Modules 7 and 8 build whatever you decide here.

## Before you arrive

| | |
|---|---|
| **Bring** | Laptop with Ptera installed, your measured loop performance from [Module 4](04-control.qmd) |
| **Read** | This page |

## Deliverable

A wing planform and a tail geometry, with the simulation output that justifies
them, carried forward into [Module 7](07-wings.qmd) and
[Module 8](08-tail-housing.qmd).

::: {.callout-important}
## To be written by the instructor

This module has **no counterpart in the manufacturing guide** --- the guide
documents the research robot's final geometry, not the design exercise. The
following need to be written from course material:

- Ptera installation and a worked example
- The provided motor power curve, and its format
- What "most efficient thrust profile" means quantitatively here, and how it is
  scored
- Constraints the students must respect so their geometry remains buildable
  with the frame from [Module 5](05-frame-crank.qmd) --- span limits, root
  fitting, mass budget
- Whether teams may deviate from the reference wing, and by how much
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint --- TA sign-off

A geometry chosen, with simulation evidence, and confirmed buildable against
the frame and wing-root hardware.
:::
